claims.statement: Talon is experimental, and scheduled cron invocations are unattended: the host invokes them without approval or authorization handlers, while the runtime auto-rejects approval interrupts for requests marked `trigger: "cron"`.

Each scheduler tick first sweeps finished records, then claims due jobs by persisting their advanced next-run state before invocation; after a result it records success or error, suppresses empty or `[SILENT]` output, and changes the outcome to error if delivery fails.

The scheduler processes due jobs sequentially but survives an unexpected tick failure; the host runs each job on a locked dedicated cron thread with a timeout and interruption recovery, and sends non-silent output to the recorded origin channel.

Cron jobs can persist up to eight validated, order-preserving, de-duplicated skill names; a scheduled host invocation forwards them as `pinned_skills`, while the runtime accepts such metadata only for cron-triggered requests and injects it into the model payload.

For each scheduled fire, Talon locks a stable per-job cron root but creates a unique run conversation ID, so scheduled runs are serialized per job while starting with fresh checkpointed history rather than continuing a prior scheduled prompt.

In attended chat, `BackgroundSubagents` creates in-memory conversation-owned workers and injects their completed results into a later main-agent turn; results are acknowledged only after that turn completes, are requeued when the host discards an undelivered reply, and are dropped after three failed result-delivery attempts.

Detached chat subagents are limited to 128 stored jobs and a configurable shared running-worker limit, have a one-hour timeout and 64,000-character results, and run without inheriting the authorization handler.

For cron-triggered turns, delegation is inline rather than detached: it returns work in the same turn, creates no background job, hides inspection, messaging, listing, and cancellation tools, queues behind a separate four-slot limit, and turns timeout or failure into safe tool errors.

Runtime shutdown cancels background workers before closing graph or checkpoint resources; if workers outlive the cancellation wait it raises and leaves those resources open, while the host logs component-stop failures and continues its shutdown sequence.

Cron-store locks coordinate complete reads and mutations only among store instances in the current process; they do not coordinate other processes, execution, or delivery, so a jobs file requires a single owner process.
The CLI installs `PersistentCronScheduler` only when channels are configured, wiring the cron store to `TalonHost.run_scheduled_job` and a delivery callback.

Cron tools scope create, list, edit, and removal to the current origin and support relative, timezone-aware wall-clock, and five-field cron schedule forms; a job's delivery choice selects only its result target.

Remote async subagents are loaded fail-closed from `[async_subagents]` configuration: every definition requires a name, description, and graph ID, while optional URL and string headers are validated; remote runs cancel on disconnect and translate stream failures or approval interrupts into safe results.

Talon reloads only trusted assistant-home hooks for each runtime turn, validates hook interrupt identity against that turn's snapshot, thread, and prompt, and gives fresh local subagents isolated child hook identities and transcripts while retaining the parent hook snapshot.
Cron turns can read an available origin chat history scope but are excluded from writing their execution transcript to the archive; final replies are recorded only after host-confirmed delivery.

While running, the host polls ready background-subagent results, skips conversations that are locked, active, blocked, superseded, or not ready, and starts an unattended `background_delivery` follow-up only when it can claim a capped exponential-backoff retry slot; that follow-up receives neither approval nor authorization handler.

Attended conversations can inspect and cooperatively guide only their own subagents: inspection returns final result plus bounded lifecycle/model/tool metadata and message receipt IDs/statuses, while its activity omits reasoning, arguments, tool outputs, and message text; guidance is bounded, accepted only for Talon-built local workers, and injected at the worker's next model boundary without interrupting active work.

`DEEPAGENTS_TALON_MAX_BACKGROUND_TASKS` configures the shared positive running-worker ceiling, and `DEEPAGENTS_TALON_INLINE_SUBAGENT_TIMEOUT` configures the positive per-delegation scheduled-inline timeout.

Fresh local subagents are compiled with the parent graph's applicable approval policy for explicitly attached tools; foreground tasks can surface those approvals to the parent, while detached tasks safely report an unmet approval and opaque precompiled subagents are refused whenever policy enforcement is required.
